# THE GAUGE CORPUS -- one file, two consumers, and neither may drift from Lean.
# Columns: vector | breadth | M | C | T | expected R/s+ (2dp)
# `expected` is NOT a hand-written constant and must never be edited to make a
# checker pass. It is what `RotGauge.gaugeF` evaluates to, and
# `checker/gauge-cross.sh` FAILS in the lean job if this column and Lean
# disagree -- so the only legitimate way to change a number here is to change
# the model and re-derive it.
# Why the file exists at all: `gauge-cross.sh` needs a built Lean workspace, so
# in the `checkers` job it could only ever print
# "SKIPPED: no built Lean workspace -- NOT a pass" and exit 0. That step could
# not pass on ubuntu, macos or windows -- it could only skip, on every run, for
# the whole cycle. An instrument that cannot pass is not an instrument.
# Splitting the arms fixes it honestly rather than by deletion:
#   * the LEAN arm is platform-independent (the same .olean everywhere), so the
#     lean job verifies Lean == hook == this file, once;
#   * the HOOK arm is NOT (awk, shell, and a decimal comma under some locales),
#     so `checker/gauge-hook-corpus.sh` diffs the running hook against this file
#     on all three platforms, where it can genuinely PASS and FAIL.
# Rows cover shapes that behave differently, not nine variants of one: the
# all-quiet floor, one active lens, two active lenses, everything active, and
# two rows whose modifiers are not the defaults.
